clue.text: Joke about Conservative in T. Blair ridiculously amusing thing – British system often breaking down?

indicators.note: done ridiculously, the letters are made absurd and so are scrambled into another order
one letter put in among others joins the set of letters to be rearranged
to be about something is to go round it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
the letters of the former prime minister's name with initial
sport can mean fun or something that amuses

explanation.surface: A jibe about a Tory hidden inside Tony Blair's name, mocking Britain's creaking railways and buses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservative goes in among Blair's letters before the shuffle; the rearranged block then sits inside the joke, between its U and N, and SPORT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses and trains run for everyone are notoriously unreliable in Britain, so the question mark gently mocks the national network.

clue.text: Demon bird breaking surface of perennial plant

indicators.note: something breaking a surface pushes through it, so these letters go inside
the surface of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
an imp is a small demon
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A devilish bird bursting up through the soil of a flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perennial plant' reads as one phrase, but only 'plant' defines; 'perennial' is reduced to its outside, which then wraps everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small red-flowered wildflower of fields and gardens, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: See 6
Green carpet over river, one mile ahead

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for mile
a mat is a small carpet
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A green carpet laid by a river, a mile further on.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the carpet above the river, and 'ahead' puts the one and mile at the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced or not fully developed, the sense of young and unripe.

clue.text: Touch what may be sharpened in prong

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it, between its letters

blocks.note: the musical note G can be raised to G sharp
a tine is a prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Touch a fork prong that needs sharpening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharpened' suggests a blade, but it is musical: a note that can be made sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch of something is a slight trace or hint, the same as a small tint or shade.

clue.text: Apparent offenders ending in hellfire after others saved by God

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter alone
coming after means following on in sequence, placed second
something saved is held safe inside, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
the rest means the others
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sinners spared from hellfire while others are rescued by God.
explanation.walkthrough: The theological picture hides a charade inside a deity: the others then the last letter of hellfire, all held within the war god.
explanation.definitionFit: People taken into custody are only suspected of crimes, so they are offenders in appearance until convicted.

clue.text: Mark of literature half read amid loud squawking of chicks?

indicators.note: taking half a word drops the rest of its letters
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a squab is a young pigeon, a nestling
the first half of the word, its opening two letters
a racket is a loud din

explanation.surface: Trying to read a book while chicks are squawking loudly around you.
explanation.walkthrough: The chicks' noise reads as the racket of the young pigeons: the half word goes inside the chick, and the din follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A square-shaped parenthesis is a punctuation mark used in printed text to insert editorial comments.

clue.text: Asses in that way carrying king’s daughter uphill

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece encloses another
in a down clue going uphill means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: so means in that manner
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: Donkeys carrying a princess up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Shakespeare's Lear; his daughter sits inside the two-letter word and the whole is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of central Asia, so the plural names a group of such animals.

clue.text: Cat-flaps so?

blocks.note: first meaning: a striped domestic cat
second meaning, whimsical: tabs are flaps, and the -y ending means being like that

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like a pet door; split it and read the second part as an invented adjective meaning full of tabs.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped household pet is named after striped silk, and the joke coinage treats it as having many tabs.

clue.text: Butcher giving yours truly a butt end of ham in batter

indicators.note: the butt end is the very tail, so only the final letter is kept
being put in something means going between its letters

blocks.note: the speaker referring to himself
taken as written
to tan is to beat or thrash
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A butcher handing over a piece of ham dipped in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the cooking coating, but it is the verb: to tan someone's hide is to beat them.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of flesh for eating is a straightforward description of a trader in a shop selling beef and pork.

clue.text: Rubbish plant

blocks.note: first meaning: nonsense, a British informal sense
second meaning: a garden plant with edible pink stalks

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word means nonsense, and actors murmur it on stage to mimic background chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal British term for nonsense talk and the name of a vegetable grown for its stalks.

clue.text: Gosh, 3/8 of 16 down?

indicators.note: a fraction of a word means taking only some of its letters, here three of eight

blocks.note: the answer at 16 down means two weeks, written as eight letters, of which three are taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at some sum involving another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 down is FORTNIGHT, which is TWO WEEKS: eight letters, and the fifth to seventh give EEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild interjections of surprise or alarm, so one exclamation can replace the other.

clue.text: Person encouraging Welshman to fill vacancy in Tonypandy saw application?

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so these letters are enclosed
a word left vacant has its middle emptied out, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: Rees is a common Welsh name
an urger is one who urges others on
the first and last letters of the Welsh town's name

explanation.surface: Someone urging a Welshman to apply for a job going in Tonypandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonypandy is a town in the Welsh valleys; emptied, it is just its two ends, which wrap the Welshman and the encourager.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopping and pruning trees is work done with a saw, so the craft is a use to which a saw is put.

clue.text: Lover with sensation in tool

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, someone mad about something
a cracker is something excellent, a knockout

explanation.surface: A romantic partner feeling something odd about a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover' suggests romance but means a fan, as in a fitness nut; a cracker is British slang for something sensational.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged hand implement for breaking open hard shells is a kitchen tool.

clue.text: Ginger root with cream

blocks.note: a carrot is a root vegetable
the cream is the top, the best part

explanation.surface: A recipe: ginger root served with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' wants to be the spice; it is a nickname, British slang for a red-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal nicknames for someone with red hair, the colour of the orange vegetable.

clue.text: A short riddle that seems very unlikely!

indicators.note: something short lacks its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written
to riddle is to pass through a sieve

explanation.surface: A quick puzzle whose solution seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle, but a riddle is also a coarse sieve, and to riddle soil is to sieve it.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word exclamation is a sarcastic retort expressing disbelief that something could ever happen.

clue.text: Period dedicated to uncharitable banking institution’s ending

indicators.note: banks line both sides, so one piece sits flanked by another
the ending of a word is its last letter alone

blocks.note: dedicated to means for, as in a gift for someone
tight means mean with money
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spell spent working for a stingy bank's closure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking institution' reads as a bank, but 'banking' surrounds and only the final letter of the institution is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of fourteen days is a length of time, which is what a period is.

clue.text: Chest hidden in London tree – somewhere in that city

indicators.note: something concealed within another sits inside it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an ark is a chest or coffer
the London plane is the tree lining the city's streets

explanation.surface: Treasure stowed in a tree somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'hidden in' does not signal letters running across words: it puts the chest inside the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Park Lane is a famous upmarket street in central London, so it is a place within the city named.

clue.text: Stamp nothing on wood

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, following on

blocks.note: a log is a piece of wood
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Stamping nothing onto a piece of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, one thing on another is added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp can be an identifying mark or emblem, just as a brand's design symbol is.

clue.text: Greek character after starter from Greece, certainly not cold Italian food

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the first letter is taken
coming after means placed later in the sequence

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
an emphatic refusal
C for cold, as on taps
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek refusing a cold Italian starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a dish on a menu, matching the food, but it only takes the opening letter of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: These small potato dumplings are a classic dish from Italy, often served like pasta.

clue.text: Criminal speaking French, very successful student

blocks.note: très is the French word for very
a student who passes an exam

explanation.surface: A criminal who speaks French fluently and was a star pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking French' does not describe the criminal; it tells you to put the next word into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters land unlawfully is a wrongdoer, though usually a civil rather than criminal one.

clue.text: See 28 Across
Wrinkly, I don trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman, as is señor

explanation.surface: An old person describing putting on their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like the verb to put on, but it is the Spanish gentleman's title; 'trousers' is the verb to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrinkly is British slang for an old person, and a senior is an elderly citizen.

clue.text: In the course of confab, one topic known to provide grievance

indicators.note: during the course of a stretch of text means the letters lie somewhere within it

blocks.note: runs from the end of confab through to the first letter of known

explanation.surface: During a chat, one subject comes up that causes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sits across four words, starting with the last two letters of confab and ending on the k of known.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a complaint you want to raise with someone, which is what a grievance is.

clue.text: River has run drier

blocks.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A river that has become less wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' looks like the comparative adjective but is the noun, a thing for drying.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a clothes horse, a frame on which washing is hung so it can dry.

clue.text: Country shown in chart, a little weightless?

indicators.note: less means without, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
a diagram is a chart
a gram is a small unit of weight, the part before the removal signal

explanation.surface: A nation drawn on a map, looking rather slight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weightless' seems to be one word, but split it: a little weight, then 'less' to remove it from the chart.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Get a move on, one leaving Waterloo

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Waterloo is a final crushing defeat, a downfall

explanation.surface: Hurry up, someone is departing from Waterloo station.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo seems to be the London station, but meeting your Waterloo means your ruin, after Napoleon's defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a move on is to hurry, and running is moving quickly on foot.

clue.text: Getting tired initially, man with head on recliner lying back

definitions.note: a noun here, the act of receiving

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
the head of a word is its first letter
lying back is facing the other way, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a man in chess or draughts is a piece
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man growing sleepy, leaning back in his armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a game piece, as in chessmen; 'Getting' must be read as a noun, the act of getting something.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt means the act of receiving, as in on receipt of payment, which matches getting used as a noun.

clue.text: Pull to keep secure in traction

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold onto it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to drag is to pull
to win is to secure or obtain

explanation.surface: Pulling a patient into place to keep a limb secure in traction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traction' suggests a hospital bed, but it means pulling, the noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of hauling something along, which is what drawing a cart means.

clue.text: Case of passenger resilience came with travel when forced – onto this?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters
letters forced out of shape are bent into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Train travellers' patience tested when they are herded off the train and onto something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the final words the definition: passengers forced onto a bus when the trains are not running.
explanation.definitionFit: When British lines close for engineering work, rail passengers are herded onto substitute buses running the train route.
